drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 states Foundry is an autonomous computational-systems factory whose purpose is to convert intent into verified running systems and keep actual systems aligned with intended state.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01's founding thesis holds that implementation artifacts are replaceable while the durable asset is the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, and verification obligations.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 1 and Law 2 in EV-T1-01 place intended state above artifacts and require every operation to explain, reduce, verify, or authorize the delta between actual and intended state.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 3 in EV-T1-01 forbids treating any model as canonical project memory and requires bounded, job-specific context with persistent state outside models.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 4 in EV-T1-01 requires routing work to the cheapest mechanism that can meet the required confidence, risk, and verification level.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 5 in EV-T1-01 separates generation from verification and forbids a process that creates a proposal from being its sole authority for correctness.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 7 in EV-T1-01 requires every material belief to distinguish confidence, authority to define intended state, and provenance.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 8 in EV-T1-01 forbids research from directly mutating canonical intent and requires the flow Research → Evidence → Reasoning → Authorization → Canonical State.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Both design documents open with a Status section that states whether the architecture is proposed or locked and that v1 remains frozen.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 locate the v1 defect after discovery: identical issues are emitted under several labels because durable semantic identity and governed consolidation are missing.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Both designs organize around the sentence that AI understands meaning while Foundry governs meaning, without replacing semantic reasoning with deterministic rules.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Both documents treat discovery output as disposable and interpreted governed semantic state as durable; EV-T2-01 additionally locks Foundry's role as compounding frontier intelligence into reconcilable state.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Section 5–6 in both documents reject gap-centric and semantic-state-first options and recommend hybrid Option C: discovery candidate, governed state, then gap projection.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Section 4 in both documents is the contract that AI may only propose open-ended semantic judgments and deterministic Foundry may only admit or refuse transitions.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §1.1 locks that the Intent Engine starts from any project evidence, not typed human requirements, with greenfield and brownfield converging on one semantic substrate.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Section 4.5 in both documents states when address equality becomes a deterministic referential fact; EV-T2-01 corrects that this is not eternal or model-independent semantic truth.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Section 7.2 in both documents defines identity as a Foundry-owned opaque address_id, with subject, facet, and scope as descriptors that are never equality keys.

drafts.rationale: Both designs make EQUIVALENT the only merge-eligible relation over addresses; EV-T2-01 §7.2.1 further requires non-destructive retention of both addresses and a derived representative view.
drafts.subject: SemanticAddress

drafts.rationale: Section 7.3 in both documents states claims are append-only and are never merged, rewritten, or averaged.

drafts.rationale: Section 7.4 in both documents defines an issue as the consolidated unresolved thing at one address, with at most one live issue per address.

drafts.rationale: Section 9 in both documents specifies the semantic relation set; EV-T2-01 locks the core slice to EQUIVALENT, DISTINCT, and CONFLICTS_WITH.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Section 12 in both documents defines consolidation as deterministic application of admitted relations that unions evidence and appends claims without deleting anything.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Section 13 in both documents treats conflict as first-class DISPUTED state from admitted claim-level CONFLICTS_WITH, clearable only by authority, never by consolidation.

drafts.rationale: Both designs remove GapKind from identity and assign it after consolidation over the consolidated issue, keeping any discovery gap_hypothesis advisory.

drafts.rationale: Section 25 in both documents bounds slice 1 to frozen v1 discovery, retrieval, cluster adjudication, in-memory consolidation, and late gap projection, excluding cross-run persistence.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 states Foundry's purpose as converting intent into verified running systems and keeping actual systems aligned with intended state.

value.text: Convert intent into verified running systems and continuously keep actual systems aligned with their intended state.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 founding thesis says implementation artifacts are replaceable, decisions are durable, and the durable asset is the evidence-backed system of intent and related obligations.

value.text: The evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, contracts, invariants, rationale, authority, and verification obligations; implementation artifacts are replaceable and decisions are durable.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 2 defines intended versus actual state and requires every operation to explain, reduce, verify, or authorize the delta.

value.text: Foundry continuously reasons about Delta = Actual State minus Intended State; every operation must help explain, reduce, verify, or explicitly authorize that delta.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 3 forbids treating any model as canonical project memory and requires persistent state outside models.

value.text: No model is the canonical memory of a project; persistent state lives outside models, which receive bounded compiled context and may then disappear.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 4 states the cheapest-trustworthy-executor rule and the preferred executor order.

value.text: Route work to the cheapest mechanism that can reliably satisfy the required confidence, risk, and verification level, in order: deterministic computation, cheap model worker, stronger model worker, frontier reasoning, human authority.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 5 states generation cannot certify itself and separates generation from verification.

value.text: The process that creates a proposal or artifact cannot be its sole authority for correctness; generation and verification are separate concerns.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 7 requires confidence, authority, and provenance to be independent.

value.text: Every material belief must independently distinguish confidence, authority, and provenance; a highly confident inference is still an inference unless authorized as canonical intent.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 8 states research produces evidence not truth and gives the required authorization flow.

value.text: Research cannot directly mutate canonical intent; the required flow is Research to Evidence to Reasoning to Authorization to Canonical State.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 status section states the design is proposed, awaiting architect review, not approved, and not implemented.

value.text: PROPOSED — awaiting architect review; not approved; not implemented

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 status section states locked core architecture with Task 9N amendments architect-approved and core-slice implementation authorised.

value.text: LOCKED CORE ARCHITECTURE — architect-approved; core-slice implementation authorised

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 state the v1 defect as duplicate emission without durable semantic identity or governed consolidation.

value.text: v1 discovers the right unresolved issues then emits each several times under several labels because it lacks durable semantic identity and a governed consolidation stage between discovery and emission.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 give this as the design's organising sentence.

value.text: AI understands meaning. Foundry governs meaning.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 §3 and EV-T2-01 §3.1 state that discovery output is disposable and governed semantic state is durable.

value.text: Discovery output is disposable; interpreted, governed semantic state is durable.

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §3.1 [9N LOCK] states Foundry's purpose as compounding frontier intelligence into durable governed state rather than beating one-shot discovery.

value.text: Foundry compounds frontier intelligence across evidence, time, agents, models and the software lifecycle by turning temporary semantic judgments into durable, governed and reconcilable state.

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §1.1 [9N LOCK] states the Intent Engine starts from any project evidence, not from typed requirements alone.

value.text: Any project evidence (human statements, documents, code, tests, tickets, pull requests, agent conversations, architecture, runtime observations, research, and brownfield archaeology); human-written requirements are one source among many, and greenfield and brownfield converge into the same semantic substrate.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §4.3 state this AI-versus-Foundry responsibility line.

value.text: AI may propose a state-changing semantic judgment but never apply one; deterministic Foundry may apply or refuse a transition but never originate an open-ended semantic conclusion.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §4.4 list these forbidden authoritative shortcuts.

value.text: Same subject string, same GapKind, high embedding similarity, shared source event, shared semantic ancestor, and AI confidence above a threshold must never become authoritative semantic rules; they may only decide what deserves comparison.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §4.5 treats admitted address equality as a deterministic authoritative identity rule downstream of the binding judgment.

value.text: After AI judges that a candidate binds to ADDR-x and Foundry admits that binding, the statement that two issues at ADDR-x are about the same thing becomes deterministic and authoritative.

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §4.5 [9N LOCK] corrects referential identity to current-interpretation referential fact, explicitly not eternal or semantically proven truth.

value.text: After admission, ADDR-x equality is a deterministic referential fact under the current admitted interpretation only; it is not a new semantic inference, not eternal truth, and not proof the binding was semantically correct, and the binding may later be superseded.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §5–§6 recommend Option C and reject Options A and B for v2's first form.

value.text: Option C hybrid: SemanticIssueCandidate discovery, then retrieval, AI adjudication, deterministic admission, persistent semantic state, late GapKind classification, and gap projection

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §7.2 state that address_id is identity and descriptors are never keys.

value.text: Durable identity is a Foundry-owned opaque address_id; subject, facet, and scope are human-readable descriptors, never keys, and Foundry never compares those descriptors for equality to decide identity.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §7.3 state claims are append-only and never merged, rewritten, or averaged.

value.text: Claims are append-only and are never merged, rewritten, or averaged.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §7.4 state one address holds at most one live issue.

value.text: One address holds at most one live issue.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §9 and §12 specify EQUIVALENT merges addresses by binding a candidate to the live issue's address_id.

value.text: EQUIVALENT is the only merge-eligible relation and merges addresses not claims, including binding a candidate onto a live issue's address_id.

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §7.2.1 and §12 [9N LOCK] require non-destructive equivalence: both addresses retained and a representative view derived.

value.text: If two existing addresses are judged EQUIVALENT, Foundry does not delete either, rewrite historical references, or copy claims; it records the judgment and derives a current representative view that is reversible by supersession.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §9 specifies these seven relations for v2.

value.text: EQUIVALENT, NARROWS, CONSEQUENCE_OF, BUNDLES, CONFLICTS_WITH, OVERLAPS, DISTINCT

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §9 [9N LOCK] restricts the implemented core-slice vocabulary to EQUIVALENT, DISTINCT, and CONFLICTS_WITH.

value.text: Core slice: EQUIVALENT, DISTINCT, CONFLICTS_WITH; NARROWS, CONSEQUENCE_OF, BUNDLES, and OVERLAPS remain designed but unbuilt

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §11 specify these retrieval sources and exclusions.

value.text: Cheap, approximate, non-authoritative retrieval from bound addresses, then semantic ancestry overlap, then lexical or embedding hints; source-event overlap alone and confidence are not used.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §12 define consolidation as merging addresses and unioning evidence while never merging claims.

value.text: Deterministic application of admitted AI relationship judgments to produce, per semantic address, one live issue carrying the union of contributing evidence, claims, provenance and relations without deleting anything; claims are appended never merged.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §8 and §13 require conflicts to be preserved as DISPUTED rather than collapsed.

value.text: A conflict is first-class state: admitted claim-level CONFLICTS_WITH sets the issue DISPUTED; consolidation cannot clear DISPUTED; only an authority event can settle, marking losing claims SUPERSEDED without deleting them.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §15 specify that materiality is judged over compiled existing decisions, authority, and supersession, not isolated prose.

value.text: The issue with its claims and evidence, existing canonical decisions at or near the address, relevant authority records, supersession history, and current scope and closure state.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §16 keep those four grounding verdicts and cut INSUFFICIENT.

value.text: SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, NOT_SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED; INSUFFICIENT cut

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §17 assign GapKind late and remove it from identity.

value.text: Assigned after consolidation by AI over the consolidated issue, and removed from identity entirely; discovery may emit only an advisory non-binding gap_hypothesis.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §17 state Gap is a projection and the durable object is the issue at an address.

value.text: projected view, not a durable record; durable object is the issue at an address

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §17.1 [9N LOCK] requires scoped, never global, closure evaluation.

value.text: Closure is always evaluated for a scope and never assumed globally; one scope may proceed while another remains blocked.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §19 treats blast radius as recomputing projections from touched addresses and defers dependency-graph traversal as YAGNI.

value.text: Correction is append-plus-supersede; affected projections are recomputed from the address set touched by the superseded judgment, and dependency-graph traversal is not designed.

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §19.1 [9N LOCK] requires a DERIVED_FROM primitive and transitive stale marking in the current view.

value.text: A generic append-only DERIVED_FROM primitive; when an admitted semantic basis is superseded, every transitive descendant is marked STALE/NEEDS_RECONCILIATION in the current view without rewriting historical records.

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §20.1 [9N LOCK] specifies risk-based admission routing with those four outcomes and forbids confidence-as-authority.

value.text: APPLY, REQUIRE_SECOND_LENS, REQUIRE_HUMAN, or REJECT; confidence never confers authority and independence is testable via reasoner fingerprint

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §23 presents single-pass cleanliness as the primary testable claim and withholds the lifecycle claim.

value.text: Primary claim is single-pass: preserve critical semantic recall while strictly improving useful precision, redundancy rate, and unsupported rate versus one-shot frontier analysis; the lifecycle persistence claim is explicitly not yet tested.

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §23.1 [9N LOCK] demotes single-pass cleanliness to a subsystem gate and names longitudinal validation as the primary target.

value.text: Single-pass cleanliness is a subsystem quality gate, not the final validation claim; primary validation must ultimately be longitudinal across evolving evidence, conflict preservation, resolution, blast radius, and model/agent takeover.

drafts.rationale: Both EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 §25 specify this in-scope and out-of-scope slice-1 boundary.

value.text: Frozen v1 discovery adapted to SemanticIssueCandidate, then deterministic retrieval, bounded AI cluster adjudication, deterministic consolidation, late classification and gap projection; in-memory for a single run with the full invariant set; not included: cross-run persistence, event-store integration, supersession machinery, embedding retrieval, materiality-from-canonical-decisions, or human escalation.

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §25.1 [9N LOCK] defines this explicit versioned scoped handoff contract and does not implement its consumer.

value.text: A versioned, scoped Intent-to-Decision handoff for one scope carrying project and scope identity, semantic-state revision, representative addresses, current claims and conflicts, evidence and authority state, relevant supersession, stale-dependency information, and scoped closure, pointing to durable truth by stable ID rather than duplicating the ledger.
